why: Multiple searches confirm the chromatic number of biplanar graphs is still bounded between 9 (Sulanke 1980) and 12 (Ringel 1959), unchanged since before the snapshot; a 2025-ish GitHub repo gives a computer-assisted proof of 9-colorability for biplanar graphs up to 18 vertices, which reconfirms the existing lower bound on small cases rather than improving it, and Epoch AI lists this as an open FrontierMath challenge still awaiting a chromatic-number-10 construction.

found.title: Computer-assisted proof of nine-colorability for biplanar graphs on at most 18 vertices
found.note: GitHub repo verifying existing 9-colorability lower bound holds for small (<=18 vertex) biplanar graphs; does not construct a chromatic-10 example or change known bounds.
